implement-cicd-in-fabric.Q: What is the purpose of lifecycle management in Microsoft Fabric?
implement-cicd-in-fabric.A: To incrementally release and integrate Fabric item changes and move those changes through a deployment process for testing and release.

implement-cicd-in-fabric.Q: Which tools can be integrated with Microsoft Fabric for source control?
implement-cicd-in-fabric.A: GitHub and Azure DevOps.

implement-cicd-in-fabric.Q: What are the key components of lifecycle management in Microsoft Fabric?
implement-cicd-in-fabric.A: Deployment pipelines and source control integration.

implement-cicd-in-fabric.Q: What is the role of deployment pipelines in Microsoft Fabric?
implement-cicd-in-fabric.A: To facilitate continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) by managing the deployment process.

implement-cicd-in-fabric.Q: What is the purpose of continuous integration in software development?
implement-cicd-in-fabric.A: To frequently commit code to a shared branch, validate changes through automated builds and tests, and identify conflicts early in the development process.

implement-cicd-in-fabric.Q: What does continuous delivery involve in the CI/CD process?
implement-cicd-in-fabric.A: Deploying code to a staging environment for automated testing before releasing it into production.

implement-cicd-in-fabric.Q: What is continuous deployment?
implement-cicd-in-fabric.A: A process that automatically releases updates into production environments through structured deployment stages after passing automated tests.

implement-cicd-in-fabric.Q: What tool in Microsoft Fabric is used for version control and collaboration in CI/CD?
implement-cicd-in-fabric.A: Git.

implement-cicd-in-fabric.Q: What are Fabric deployment pipelines used for?
implement-cicd-in-fabric.A: To promote code changes to different environments such as development, test, and production.

implement-cicd-in-fabric.Q: How can automation of deployment or integration be implemented in Microsoft Fabric?
implement-cicd-in-fabric.A: Using Fabric REST APIs.

implement-cicd-in-fabric.Q: What is the purpose of version control in software development?
implement-cicd-in-fabric.A: Version control manages changes to code over time, allowing tracking of revisions, collaborative development, and reverting to prior versions if needed.

implement-cicd-in-fabric.Q: Which version control systems are supported in Microsoft Fabric?
implement-cicd-in-fabric.A: GitHub and Azure DevOps.

implement-cicd-in-fabric.Q: What is a branch in the context of version control systems?
implement-cicd-in-fabric.A: A branch is a copy of a code repository that allows independent work on code separate from the main version.

implement-cicd-in-fabric.Q: At what level is version control integration implemented in Microsoft Fabric?
implement-cicd-in-fabric.A: At the workspace level.

implement-cicd-in-fabric.Q: What is a best practice for developing in a shared Fabric workspace?
implement-cicd-in-fabric.A: Develop in an isolated workspace outside of the shared, live workspace to avoid affecting other users.

implement-cicd-in-fabric.Q: What is the first step in implementing Git integration in Microsoft Fabric?
implement-cicd-in-fabric.A: Set up a Git repository in GitHub or Azure DevOps.

implement-cicd-in-fabric.Q: What does the Git status column in a Fabric workspace indicate?
implement-cicd-in-fabric.A: It indicates the synchronization state of items in the workspace compared to the items in the remote branch.

implement-cicd-in-fabric.Q: What is the purpose of creating a dedicated branch for development in Microsoft Fabric?
implement-cicd-in-fabric.A: To isolate feature development work from the main branch, allowing multiple developers to work without affecting the main branch.

implement-cicd-in-fabric.Q: What are deployment pipelines in Microsoft Fabric?
implement-cicd-in-fabric.A: Deployment pipelines in Microsoft Fabric help deploy items across different environments like development, test, and production, allowing content to be developed and tested before reaching end users.

implement-cicd-in-fabric.Q: What are the two methods to create a deployment pipeline in Microsoft Fabric?
implement-cicd-in-fabric.A: Deployment pipelines can be created using the Workspaces icon on the left navigation pane or the Create deployment pipeline icon at the top of a workspace.

implement-cicd-in-fabric.Q: What is the purpose of assigning a workspace to a pipeline stage in Microsoft Fabric?
implement-cicd-in-fabric.A: Assigning a workspace to a pipeline stage is necessary to deploy content to that stage within the deployment pipeline.

implement-cicd-in-fabric.Q: What is the typical sequence of stages in a deployment pipeline?
implement-cicd-in-fabric.A: The typical sequence of stages in a deployment pipeline is Development, Test, and Production.

implement-cicd-in-fabric.Q: How can deployment pipelines in Microsoft Fabric be integrated with Git?
implement-cicd-in-fabric.A: Deployment pipelines can be integrated with Git by connecting the Development workspace to a Git repository and branch, using Git for version control during development, and using the pipeline to promote content to Test and Production environments.

implement-cicd-in-fabric.Q: What does REST API stand for?
implement-cicd-in-fabric.A: Representational State Transfer Application Programming Interface.

implement-cicd-in-fabric.Q: What are two advantages of using Fabric REST APIs?
implement-cicd-in-fabric.A: Automating repeat processes with consistency and seamless integration with other systems and applications.

implement-cicd-in-fabric.Q: What are Fabric CI/CD REST APIs used for?
implement-cicd-in-fabric.A: They are used for deployment pipelines and Git integration.

implement-cicd-in-fabric.Q: What can you do with the Git status API in Fabric REST APIs?
implement-cicd-in-fabric.A: You can see which items have incoming changes and which items have changes that weren't yet committed to Git.

implement-cicd-in-fabric.Q: What does the 'List Deployment Pipeline Stage Items' API do?
implement-cicd-in-fabric.A: It returns the supported items from the workspace assigned to the specified stage of the specified deployment pipeline.

implement-cicd-in-fabric.Q: What does the 'Deploy Stage Content' API do?
implement-cicd-in-fabric.A: It deploys items from the specified stage of the specified deployment pipeline.

monitor-fabric-items.Q: What tool in Microsoft Fabric allows you to track the status of activities and investigate failures?
monitor-fabric-items.A: The monitoring hub.

monitor-fabric-items.Q: What can Activator in Microsoft Fabric do when a Fabric job event occurs?
monitor-fabric-items.A: Activator can automatically trigger actions such as sending an alert, posting a Teams message, or running a notebook.

monitor-fabric-items.Q: What is an example of a Fabric job event that Activator can respond to?
monitor-fabric-items.A: A pipeline failure or a notebook error.

monitor-fabric-items.Q: Why is monitoring important for data engineering teams in Microsoft Fabric?
monitor-fabric-items.A: Monitoring helps detect failures or slowdowns in scheduled pipelines, dataflows, and notebooks, preventing downstream effects like stale data and incomplete information.

monitor-fabric-items.Q: What is the purpose of monitoring in Microsoft Fabric?
monitor-fabric-items.A: Monitoring in Microsoft Fabric is used to collect data about system activities to determine whether they succeed, fail, or degrade over time.

monitor-fabric-items.Q: Why is monitoring important in a typical Fabric workspace?
monitor-fabric-items.A: Monitoring is important because it helps detect failures or delays in dependent activities, preventing downstream issues and ensuring data freshness.

monitor-fabric-items.Q: What are some key metrics to monitor for Dataflow Gen2?
monitor-fabric-items.A: Key metrics include start time, end time, duration, and status of the dataflow.

monitor-fabric-items.Q: What should you monitor in Spark jobs and notebooks?
monitor-fabric-items.A: Monitor job progress, execution duration, and Spark logs to identify issues like data skew or inefficient transformations.

monitor-fabric-items.Q: What is a recommended practice for establishing a monitoring baseline?
monitor-fabric-items.A: Track metrics consistently, define normal behavior, set up notifications, investigate anomalies promptly, and review baselines periodically.

monitor-fabric-items.Q: What is the purpose of the monitoring hub in Microsoft Fabric?
monitor-fabric-items.A: The monitoring hub provides a centralized interface to view and manage activity data across a workspace, allowing users to monitor the status of pipelines, dataflows, and notebooks.

monitor-fabric-items.Q: How can you access the monitoring hub in Microsoft Fabric?
monitor-fabric-items.A: You can access the monitoring hub by selecting 'Monitor' from the navigation pane on the left side of the Fabric portal.

monitor-fabric-items.Q: What does the 'Succeeded' status indicate in the monitoring hub?
monitor-fabric-items.A: The 'Succeeded' status indicates that the activity completed without errors.

monitor-fabric-items.Q: How can you view historical runs for a specific activity in the monitoring hub?
monitor-fabric-items.A: To view historical runs, hover over the activity name, select 'More options' (three dots), and then select 'Historical runs'.

monitor-fabric-items.Q: What is the purpose of workspace monitoring in Microsoft Fabric?
monitor-fabric-items.A: Workspace monitoring stores raw diagnostic logs and metrics in an Eventhouse database for advanced analysis and long-term performance monitoring.

monitor-fabric-items.Q: What role is required to configure failure notifications in the monitoring hub?
monitor-fabric-items.A: You need at least the Contributor role in the workspace to configure failure notifications.

monitor-fabric-items.Q: What type of data does workspace monitoring collect in Microsoft Fabric?
monitor-fabric-items.A: Workspace monitoring collects diagnostic logs and metrics from Fabric items and stores them in an Eventhouse database.

monitor-fabric-items.Q: How long does workspace monitoring retain data in Microsoft Fabric?
monitor-fabric-items.A: Workspace monitoring retains data for 30 days.

monitor-fabric-items.Q: What is the primary purpose of Activator in Microsoft Fabric?
monitor-fabric-items.A: Activator automates responses to Fabric job events by notifying the right people or triggering follow-up actions without waiting for human intervention.

monitor-fabric-items.Q: What types of Fabric job events can Activator act on?
monitor-fabric-items.A: Activator can act on events such as Job created, Job failed, Job succeeded, and Job status changed.

monitor-fabric-items.Q: How does Activator connect to Fabric job events?
monitor-fabric-items.A: Activator connects to Fabric job events through the Real-Time hub.

monitor-fabric-items.Q: What is the difference between Activator and the Schedule failures page in Microsoft Fabric?
monitor-fabric-items.A: Schedule failures provides simple, centrally managed email alerts for scheduled failures, while Activator provides richer notification channels and can trigger follow-up actions.

monitor-fabric-items.Q: What are the available actions Activator can perform when a condition is met?
monitor-fabric-items.A: Activator can send an email, post a Teams message, or run a Fabric activity such as a pipeline, notebook, dataflow, spark job, or function.

monitor-fabric-items.Q: What is the key differentiator of Activator compared to Schedule failures notifications?
monitor-fabric-items.A: Activator can trigger follow-up actions, such as running a Fabric activity, in response to job events.

monitor-fabric-items.Q: When should you use Activator instead of the Schedule failures page?
monitor-fabric-items.A: Use Activator when you need richer notification channels, want to react to job success as well as failure, or need to trigger follow-up actions.

monitor-fabric-items.Q: What is the quickest way to connect Activator to a job event in Microsoft Fabric?
monitor-fabric-items.A: The quickest way is through the Real-Time hub, using the Set alert wizard.

secure-data-access-in-fabric.Q: What are the three levels of access evaluation in Microsoft Fabric?
secure-data-access-in-fabric.A: Microsoft Entra ID authentication, Fabric access, and Data security.

secure-data-access-in-fabric.Q: What does the Microsoft Entra ID authentication level check?
secure-data-access-in-fabric.A: It checks whether the user can authenticate with Microsoft Entra ID.

secure-data-access-in-fabric.Q: What does the Fabric access level check?
secure-data-access-in-fabric.A: It checks whether the user can access Fabric.

secure-data-access-in-fabric.Q: What does the Data security level check?
secure-data-access-in-fabric.A: It checks whether the user can perform the requested action on a table or file.

secure-data-access-in-fabric.Q: What are the four primary access controls within the Data security level?
secure-data-access-in-fabric.A: Workspace roles, Item permissions, Compute or granular permissions, and OneLake security.

secure-data-access-in-fabric.Q: When should you use Workspace roles?
secure-data-access-in-fabric.A: When a user needs broad access to collaborate across multiple items in a workspace.

secure-data-access-in-fabric.Q: When should you use Item permissions?
secure-data-access-in-fabric.A: When a user only needs access to one or two specific items, not the whole workspace.

secure-data-access-in-fabric.Q: What is the purpose of OneLake security?
secure-data-access-in-fabric.A: To grant access to specific tables or folders within a Fabric item, restricting access to only specific data.

secure-data-access-in-fabric.Q: What is the purpose of workspace roles in Microsoft Fabric?
secure-data-access-in-fabric.A: Workspace roles are used to grant broad access to all items within a workspace for collaboration purposes.

secure-data-access-in-fabric.Q: Which workspace role allows a user to create, view, and modify all content in a workspace but not share or manage permissions?
secure-data-access-in-fabric.A: The Contributor role.

secure-data-access-in-fabric.Q: How can you assign a workspace role to a user in Microsoft Fabric?
secure-data-access-in-fabric.A: In the workspace, select 'Manage access', enter the user's name or email address, select the workspace role to assign, and select 'Add'.

secure-data-access-in-fabric.Q: What is the principle of least privilege in the context of Microsoft Fabric permissions?
secure-data-access-in-fabric.A: It means granting users the minimum level of access they need to perform their tasks.

secure-data-access-in-fabric.Q: What permissions can be granted when sharing a lakehouse in Microsoft Fabric?
secure-data-access-in-fabric.A: Read all SQL endpoint data, Read all Apache Spark and subscribe to events, and Build reports on the default semantic model.

secure-data-access-in-fabric.Q: What does granting 'Read all Apache Spark and subscribe to events' permission for a lakehouse do?
secure-data-access-in-fabric.A: It allows reading lakehouse data through Apache Spark and OneLake APIs and adds the recipient to the lakehouse's DefaultReader OneLake security role.

secure-data-access-in-fabric.Q: What are the three T-SQL commands used to apply granular permissions in a lakehouse?
secure-data-access-in-fabric.A: GRANT, DENY, and REVOKE.

secure-data-access-in-fabric.Q: What are the four components of a OneLake security role?
secure-data-access-in-fabric.A: Data, Permission, Members, and Constraints.

secure-data-access-in-fabric.Q: Who can create or modify OneLake security roles?
secure-data-access-in-fabric.A: Workspace Admin and Member roles.

secure-data-access-in-fabric.Q: What is the purpose of the DefaultReader role in a lakehouse?
secure-data-access-in-fabric.A: It provides read access to all data in the lakehouse when shared with the 'Read all Apache Spark and subscribe to events' permission.

secure-data-access-in-fabric.Q: What should you do when assigning a user to a custom OneLake security role?
secure-data-access-in-fabric.A: Remove them from the DefaultReader role to prevent full read access through the default role.

secure-data-access-in-fabric.Q: What are the two permission levels that can be assigned in a OneLake security role?
secure-data-access-in-fabric.A: Read and ReadWrite.

secure-data-access-in-fabric.Q: What is the difference between OneLake security and T-SQL permissions?
secure-data-access-in-fabric.A: OneLake security uses a role-based access control model, while T-SQL permissions are applied using Data Control Language commands.

secure-data-access-in-fabric.Q: What role is required to assign workspace roles in Microsoft Fabric?
secure-data-access-in-fabric.A: The Workspace Admin role.

secure-data-access-in-fabric.Q: How many user accounts are required to complete the exercise on securing data access in Microsoft Fabric?
secure-data-access-in-fabric.A: Two user accounts.

secure-data-access-in-fabric.Q: What is the purpose of the second user account in the Microsoft Fabric data access exercise?
secure-data-access-in-fabric.A: To be assigned permissions throughout the lab.

secure-data-access-in-fabric.Q: What type of Microsoft Fabric capacity is needed to complete the exercise on securing data access?
secure-data-access-in-fabric.A: A Fabric paid or trial capacity.

administer-fabric.Q: What is the top level of the Microsoft Fabric hierarchy?
administer-fabric.A: The tenant, which represents the entire Fabric environment.

administer-fabric.Q: What does a capacity in Microsoft Fabric represent?
administer-fabric.A: A dedicated compute and storage resource that powers Fabric workloads.

administer-fabric.Q: What is the purpose of a domain in Microsoft Fabric?
administer-fabric.A: To logically group workspaces and enforce governance boundaries.

administer-fabric.Q: Who manages items such as lakehouses, notebooks, and reports in Microsoft Fabric?
administer-fabric.A: Workspace admins.

administer-fabric.Q: What is the role of a Fabric admin in Microsoft Fabric?
administer-fabric.A: To control tenant settings, manage all capacities and domains, and assign other admins.

administer-fabric.Q: What tool does a Fabric admin primarily use to configure tenant settings and manage capacities?
administer-fabric.A: The Fabric admin portal.

administer-fabric.Q: Which admin role is responsible for monitoring capacity performance in Microsoft Fabric?
administer-fabric.A: Capacity admin.

administer-fabric.Q: What is the Microsoft Entra ID role equivalent to the Fabric admin role?
administer-fabric.A: Power BI Administrator.

administer-fabric.Q: What is the purpose of tenant settings in Microsoft Fabric?
administer-fabric.A: Tenant settings provide fine-grained control over which Fabric features are available to users in an organization.

administer-fabric.Q: What is the main Fabric on/off switch in tenant settings?
administer-fabric.A: The 'Users can create Fabric items' setting.

administer-fabric.Q: What is the purpose of domains in Microsoft Fabric?
administer-fabric.A: Domains create governance boundaries that reflect an organization's structure, allowing different policies to be applied without affecting access control.

administer-fabric.Q: How can workspaces be assigned to domains in Microsoft Fabric?
administer-fabric.A: Workspaces can be assigned to domains by workspace name (using pattern matching) or by workspace admin.

administer-fabric.Q: What is the role of domain admins in Microsoft Fabric?
administer-fabric.A: Domain admins manage workspaces within their domain, override certain tenant settings, and designate domain contributors.

administer-fabric.Q: What is the purpose of delegating tenant settings to domain admins?
administer-fabric.A: Delegating tenant settings allows domain admins to customize governance policies for their domains while maintaining the broader governance framework.

administer-fabric.Q: Why might you assign development workspaces to a separate capacity in Microsoft Fabric?
administer-fabric.A: To prevent development activities from consuming resources and affecting the performance of production workloads.

administer-fabric.Q: What are the two types of licenses in Microsoft Fabric?
administer-fabric.A: Capacity licenses and per-user licenses.

administer-fabric.Q: What does a Fabric Free license allow a user to do?
administer-fabric.A: Create and share non-Power BI Fabric items in workspaces on an F capacity.

administer-fabric.Q: What license is required to create and share Power BI content in Microsoft Fabric?
administer-fabric.A: Power BI Pro or Power BI Premium Per User (PPU).

administer-fabric.Q: What is the significance of the F64 capacity in Microsoft Fabric licensing?
administer-fabric.A: Users with a Free license can view Power BI reports and dashboards if they have a viewer role on the workspace.

administer-fabric.Q: How are licenses typically assigned in Microsoft Fabric?
administer-fabric.A: Licenses are assigned using Microsoft 365 admin center, often through group-based assignments.

administer-fabric.Q: What is the recommended pattern for distributing Fabric content to large audiences?
administer-fabric.A: Using workspace apps to provide read-only access to reports and dashboards.

administer-fabric.Q: What role should be assigned to users who need read-only access to a workspace's contents?
administer-fabric.A: The Viewer role.

administer-fabric.Q: What must be configured to enable external sharing of dashboards in Microsoft Fabric?
administer-fabric.A: Tenant settings under Export and sharing settings, specifying allowed security groups for external sharing.

administer-fabric.Q: What is the purpose of the monitoring hub in Microsoft Fabric?
administer-fabric.A: The monitoring hub provides a centralized view of Fabric job execution health across the tenant, allowing users to monitor job statuses and troubleshoot failures.

administer-fabric.Q: What kind of information can be filtered in the monitoring hub?
administer-fabric.A: The monitoring hub can be filtered by status, item type, start time, the user who submitted the job, and location (workspace).

administer-fabric.Q: What is the admin monitoring workspace used for in Microsoft Fabric?
administer-fabric.A: The admin monitoring workspace is used to track platform-wide usage and adoption trends, providing insights into which features are being used and by whom.

administer-fabric.Q: What does the Microsoft Fabric Capacity Metrics app help visualize?
administer-fabric.A: The Microsoft Fabric Capacity Metrics app helps visualize CU consumption across a capacity, identifying trends and workloads consuming the most capacity.

administer-fabric.Q: What action can an admin take to save costs on non-production capacities in Microsoft Fabric?
administer-fabric.A: An admin can pause non-production capacities to save costs when they are not in use, such as overnight or over weekends.

administer-fabric.Q: What information do audit logs in Microsoft Fabric provide?
administer-fabric.A: Audit logs record user activities, such as who viewed or exported a report, shared content externally, modified permissions, or deleted items.

administer-fabric.Q: What are the two types of endorsements available for Fabric items?
administer-fabric.A: The two types of endorsements are Promoted, which can be applied by workspace members, and Certified, which requires formal review by an authorized certifier.

administer-fabric.Q: What does the Govern tab in the OneLake catalog provide?
administer-fabric.A: The Govern tab provides a governance snapshot of the tenant, including sensitivity label coverage, endorsement coverage, and recommended governance actions.

discover-data-onelake.Q: What is the main storage layer used in Microsoft Fabric?
discover-data-onelake.A: OneLake.

discover-data-onelake.Q: What tool in Microsoft Fabric allows users to browse and find existing data across an organization?
discover-data-onelake.A: The OneLake catalog.

discover-data-onelake.Q: What feature in Microsoft Fabric enables the discovery of streaming data sources?
discover-data-onelake.A: The Real-Time hub.

discover-data-onelake.Q: What problem does Microsoft Fabric aim to solve in traditional analytics environments?
discover-data-onelake.A: The scattering of data across separate storage accounts, databases, and file systems, leading to duplication and inconsistency.

discover-data-onelake.Q: What can be created in Microsoft Fabric to connect to external data sources?
discover-data-onelake.A: Shortcuts.

discover-data-onelake.Q: What is the foundational storage layer of Microsoft Fabric's analytics platform?
discover-data-onelake.A: OneLake.

discover-data-onelake.Q: What type of data lake is OneLake in Microsoft Fabric?
discover-data-onelake.A: A tenant-wide data lake.

discover-data-onelake.Q: What is the default table format used by OneLake?
discover-data-onelake.A: Delta Lake, which stores data in open Parquet files.

discover-data-onelake.Q: How does OneLake handle data governance and security?
discover-data-onelake.A: OneLake integrates with Microsoft Purview for governance, allowing data classification, sensitivity labeling, and lineage tracking, along with access controls.

discover-data-onelake.Q: What are shortcuts in OneLake used for?
discover-data-onelake.A: Shortcuts reference data in external locations without physically copying it, allowing integration with external data sources.

discover-data-onelake.Q: What are some methods for ingesting data into OneLake?
discover-data-onelake.A: Methods include mirroring, pipelines, dataflows, streaming, and direct upload.

discover-data-onelake.Q: How does OneLake support AI workflows in Microsoft Fabric?
discover-data-onelake.A: OneLake provides a unified data catalog that AI tools like Copilot use to locate and understand relevant data for insights.

discover-data-onelake.Q: What is the purpose of the OneLake catalog in Microsoft Fabric?
discover-data-onelake.A: The OneLake catalog provides a centralized discovery experience for all data items in a Microsoft Fabric tenant, allowing users to search for and locate data across the organization.

discover-data-onelake.Q: What types of metadata does the OneLake catalog display for each data item?
discover-data-onelake.A: The OneLake catalog displays metadata such as name, type, owner, last refresh time, workspace location, sensitivity labels, and endorsement status.

discover-data-onelake.Q: What are the three endorsement levels in the OneLake catalog?
discover-data-onelake.A: The three endorsement levels are Promoted, Certified, and Master data.

discover-data-onelake.Q: What is the purpose of creating shortcuts in a lakehouse?
discover-data-onelake.A: Shortcuts allow users to reference data from other workspaces without copying or moving it, enabling real-time updates and reducing data duplication.

discover-data-onelake.Q: What are some scenarios where shortcuts might not be suitable?
discover-data-onelake.A: Shortcuts might not be suitable when a stable snapshot of data is required, when network latency affects query performance, or when compliance requires physically separate copies of data.

discover-data-onelake.Q: What can you do to verify data before creating a shortcut in a lakehouse?
discover-data-onelake.A: You can use the SQL analytics endpoint to query and validate the data using T-SQL syntax.

discover-data-onelake.Q: What information can you find on the details page of a semantic model in the OneLake catalog?
discover-data-onelake.A: The details page includes an overview tab with description, owner, refresh status, endorsement, and sensitivity labels, a tables section showing schema, a lineage tab for dependencies, and a monitor tab for refresh history.

discover-data-onelake.Q: What are some options available when creating content from a semantic model in the OneLake catalog?
discover-data-onelake.A: Options include exploring data, auto-creating a report, creating a blank report, creating from a template, creating a paginated report, and analyzing in Excel.

discover-data-onelake.Q: What is the Real-Time hub in Microsoft Fabric used for?
discover-data-onelake.A: The Real-Time hub is used for discovering and managing streaming data across Microsoft Fabric.

discover-data-onelake.Q: What types of data are displayed in the Real-Time hub?
discover-data-onelake.A: The Real-Time hub displays eventstreams and KQL tables that are actively running in your organization.

discover-data-onelake.Q: What are eventstreams in Microsoft Fabric?
discover-data-onelake.A: Eventstreams are continuous flows of data from sources like Azure Event Hubs, IoT devices, Apache Kafka, database CDC, or custom applications.

discover-data-onelake.Q: What is an eventhouse in Microsoft Fabric?
discover-data-onelake.A: An eventhouse is a container that holds one or more KQL databases, which store time- or event-based events and support fast querying using KQL.

discover-data-onelake.Q: How can you access the Real-Time hub in Microsoft Fabric?
discover-data-onelake.A: You can access the Real-Time hub by selecting 'Real-Time' from the left navigation in Fabric.

discover-data-onelake.Q: What information can you find in the details of a stream in the Real-Time hub?
discover-data-onelake.A: Stream details include the stream name, source item, item owner, workspace location, endorsement status, sensitivity labels, activity information, and last update time.

discover-data-onelake.Q: What are some actions you can perform with eventstreams in the Real-Time hub?
discover-data-onelake.A: You can view properties and data profiles, set alerts using Fabric Activator, and create shortcuts for lakehouse data.

discover-data-onelake.Q: What are some actions you can perform with KQL tables in the Real-Time hub?
discover-data-onelake.A: You can query data directly using KQL, create visualizations in Real-Time dashboards, and set alerts on query results.

get-started-lakehouses.Q: Which storage layer is a Fabric lakehouse built on?
get-started-lakehouses.A: OneLake.

get-started-lakehouses.Q: What two compute engines does a Fabric lakehouse use to process and analyze data?
get-started-lakehouses.A: Apache Spark and SQL compute engines.

get-started-lakehouses.Q: What types of data can a lakehouse handle effectively?
get-started-lakehouses.A: Both structured and unstructured data.

get-started-lakehouses.Q: What problem does a lakehouse solve compared to traditional data warehouses?
get-started-lakehouses.A: It eliminates data silos and simplifies integration by handling both structured and unstructured data in a unified platform.

get-started-lakehouses.Q: What are the two main areas of data organization in a lakehouse?
get-started-lakehouses.A: Tables and Files.

get-started-lakehouses.Q: What type of data is stored in the Tables folder of a lakehouse?
get-started-lakehouses.A: Structured, queryable data in Delta Lake tables.

get-started-lakehouses.Q: What is the purpose of the Files folder in a lakehouse?
get-started-lakehouses.A: To store raw or semi-structured data files in their native format for exploration and processing.

get-started-lakehouses.Q: What storage format do Delta Lake tables use in a lakehouse?
get-started-lakehouses.A: Delta format, stored in the underlying OneLake storage.

get-started-lakehouses.Q: What are the key features of Delta Lake tables?
get-started-lakehouses.A: ACID transactions, schema enforcement, time travel, and efficient updates and deletes.

get-started-lakehouses.Q: What is the role of the transaction log in Delta Lake tables?

get-started-lakehouses.Q: What access control features does the SQL analytics endpoint in a lakehouse support?

get-started-lakehouses.Q: How does well-structured lakehouse data benefit intelligent analytics in Microsoft Fabric?

get-started-lakehouses.Q: What are the two main storage areas in a Fabric lakehouse?

get-started-lakehouses.Q: What type of data is stored in the Tables area of a lakehouse?

get-started-lakehouses.Q: What is the default schema created when you create a lakehouse?

get-started-lakehouses.Q: What are the two modes available for working with a lakehouse?

get-started-lakehouses.Q: What are some methods to ingest data into a lakehouse?

get-started-lakehouses.Q: What is the purpose of shortcuts in a lakehouse?

get-started-lakehouses.Q: What tools can be used to transform data in a lakehouse?
get-started-lakehouses.A: Notebooks, Dataflows Gen2, and Pipelines.

get-started-lakehouses.Q: What is the advantage of schema shortcuts in a lakehouse?
get-started-lakehouses.A: They map an entire schema to a folder of Delta tables in another lakehouse or Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2, making the tables appear as local tables within the schema.

get-started-lakehouses.Q: What is the SQL analytics endpoint in a Microsoft Fabric lakehouse?
get-started-lakehouses.A: The SQL analytics endpoint provides read-only access to lakehouse tables using T-SQL queries and is automatically created with every lakehouse.

get-started-lakehouses.Q: What are some common use cases for the SQL analytics endpoint in a lakehouse?
get-started-lakehouses.A: Common use cases include ad-hoc queries, business intelligence connections, and data validation.

get-started-lakehouses.Q: What security features does the SQL analytics endpoint support?
get-started-lakehouses.A: The SQL analytics endpoint supports row-level security and column-level security.

get-started-lakehouses.Q: What are the two main methods for querying data in Spark notebooks?
get-started-lakehouses.A: The two main methods are Spark SQL for SQL-like queries and PySpark for programmatic data manipulation.

get-started-lakehouses.Q: What is the difference between Spark SQL and PySpark in Spark notebooks?
get-started-lakehouses.A: Spark SQL uses SQL syntax for querying data, while PySpark uses Python code and the DataFrame API for data manipulation.

get-started-lakehouses.Q: How does Power BI connect to lakehouse data in Microsoft Fabric?
get-started-lakehouses.A: Power BI can connect to lakehouse data by querying the SQL analytics endpoint or by creating a semantic model that references specific lakehouse tables.

get-started-lakehouses.Q: What is Direct Lake mode in Power BI?
get-started-lakehouses.A: Direct Lake mode reads data directly from Delta Lake Parquet files without importing or copying data, ensuring fast query performance and up-to-date reports.

get-started-lakehouses.Q: What is the benefit of creating a semantic model in Power BI for lakehouse data?
get-started-lakehouses.A: A semantic model defines relationships, measures, and business logic, enabling Power BI to generate visualizations and answer business questions effectively.

get-started-lakehouses.Q: What storage technology is a Microsoft Fabric lakehouse built on?
get-started-lakehouses.A: OneLake, which is based on Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2.

get-started-lakehouses.Q: What table format is used for relational objects in a Microsoft Fabric lakehouse?
get-started-lakehouses.A: The Delta Lake table format.

get-started-lakehouses.Q: What can you use to define schemas and query tables in a Microsoft Fabric lakehouse?
get-started-lakehouses.A: SQL.

get-started-data-warehouse.Q: What storage format does Microsoft Fabric's data warehouse use for its data?
get-started-data-warehouse.A: Delta format on OneLake.

get-started-data-warehouse.Q: What SQL capabilities does Microsoft Fabric's data warehouse support?
get-started-data-warehouse.A: Full transactional T-SQL capabilities, including creating tables, and inserting, updating, and deleting data.

get-started-data-warehouse.Q: What are the two types of tables fundamental to dimensional modeling?
get-started-data-warehouse.A: Fact and dimension tables.

get-started-data-warehouse.Q: What feature of Microsoft Fabric's data warehouse assists with query authoring?
get-started-data-warehouse.A: Copilot-assisted query authoring.

get-started-data-warehouse.Q: What integration does Microsoft Fabric's data warehouse have with other workloads?
get-started-data-warehouse.A: Seamless integration with other Fabric workloads through OneLake.

get-started-data-warehouse.Q: What is the primary purpose of a data warehouse?
get-started-data-warehouse.A: To consolidate data from multiple sources into a format optimized for analysis.

get-started-data-warehouse.Q: What are the four main steps involved in building a modern data warehouse?
get-started-data-warehouse.A: Data ingestion, data storage, data processing, and data analysis and delivery.

get-started-data-warehouse.Q: What is a fact table in a data warehouse?
get-started-data-warehouse.A: A table that contains numerical data for analysis, typically with a large number of rows.

get-started-data-warehouse.Q: What is a dimension table in a data warehouse?
get-started-data-warehouse.A: A table that contains descriptive information about the data in fact tables, providing context for analysis.

get-started-data-warehouse.Q: What is the difference between a surrogate key and an alternate key in a dimension table?
get-started-data-warehouse.A: A surrogate key is a unique identifier for each row in the dimension table generated by the database, while an alternate key is a natural or business key from the source system.

get-started-data-warehouse.Q: What is the purpose of a time dimension in a data warehouse?
get-started-data-warehouse.A: To provide information about the time period in which an event occurred, enabling temporal aggregation of data.

get-started-data-warehouse.Q: What is a star schema in the context of a data warehouse?
get-started-data-warehouse.A: A schema design where a fact table directly relates to dimension tables, forming a star-like structure.

get-started-data-warehouse.Q: What is a snowflake schema in the context of a data warehouse?
get-started-data-warehouse.A: A schema design where dimension tables are normalized into multiple related tables, creating a more complex structure.

get-started-data-warehouse.Q: What is a Fabric data warehouse built on?
get-started-data-warehouse.A: OneLake.

get-started-data-warehouse.Q: What format is used to store data in a Fabric data warehouse?
get-started-data-warehouse.A: Delta format.

get-started-data-warehouse.Q: What SQL capabilities does a Fabric data warehouse support?
get-started-data-warehouse.A: Full T-SQL capabilities, including DDL and DML statements with ACID compliance.

get-started-data-warehouse.Q: What is the difference between a Fabric warehouse and a SQL analytics endpoint in terms of data writing?
get-started-data-warehouse.A: A Fabric warehouse supports data writing (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, MERGE), while a SQL analytics endpoint does not.

get-started-data-warehouse.Q: What command can be used to bulk load data into a Fabric data warehouse from external files?
get-started-data-warehouse.A: The COPY INTO command.

get-started-data-warehouse.Q: What is the purpose of staging tables in a Fabric data warehouse?
get-started-data-warehouse.A: To temporarily hold raw data before transforming and loading it into final dimension and fact tables.

get-started-data-warehouse.Q: What is a table clone in a Fabric data warehouse?
get-started-data-warehouse.A: A zero-copy table that references the same underlying data files without duplicating the data.

get-started-data-warehouse.Q: What is a common use case for table clones in a Fabric data warehouse?
get-started-data-warehouse.A: Development and testing, data recovery, and preserving data for historical reporting.

get-started-data-warehouse.Q: What are the two tools provided by a Fabric data warehouse for exploring and shaping data?
get-started-data-warehouse.A: The SQL query editor and the Visual query editor.

get-started-data-warehouse.Q: What features does the SQL query editor provide for writing T-SQL queries?
get-started-data-warehouse.A: It provides IntelliSense, code completion, syntax highlighting, client-side parsing, and validation.

get-started-data-warehouse.Q: What is the purpose of the Visual query editor in a Fabric data warehouse?
get-started-data-warehouse.A: It provides a no-code approach to query data, allowing users to drag tables onto a canvas and apply transformations visually.

get-started-data-warehouse.Q: What is the function of a view in a Fabric data warehouse?
get-started-data-warehouse.A: A view defines a saved query that can be referenced like a table, standardizing data access and simplifying analysis.

get-started-data-warehouse.Q: What is the purpose of stored procedures in a Fabric data warehouse?
get-started-data-warehouse.A: Stored procedures contain T-SQL logic for repeatable transformation tasks, such as loading staging data into final tables or applying business rules.

get-started-data-warehouse.Q: How can views and stored procedures improve the accessibility of data for AI-powered tools?
get-started-data-warehouse.A: They standardize data access, making it easier for tools like Copilot and Fabric IQ data agents to query data accurately.

get-started-data-warehouse.Q: What problem does data modeling solve in a Microsoft Fabric warehouse?
get-started-data-warehouse.A: It embeds structure, business logic, and documentation directly into the warehouse, eliminating the need for consumers to figure out relationships, aggregation logic, and column meanings on their own.

get-started-data-warehouse.Q: Why is it important to prepare data for consumption in a data warehouse?
get-started-data-warehouse.A: To surface only relevant data, make it understandable, and improve the consumer experience by hiding internal objects, renaming columns, and adding descriptions.

get-started-data-warehouse.Q: What is the purpose of defining relationships between tables in a data warehouse?
get-started-data-warehouse.A: To enable filtering, grouping, and aggregation across tables, and to eliminate the need for consumers to write explicit JOIN logic.

get-started-data-warehouse.Q: What are the two important properties of table relationships in a star schema?
get-started-data-warehouse.A: Cardinality and cross-filter direction.

get-started-data-warehouse.Q: What is the role of views in standardizing data access for T-SQL consumers?
get-started-data-warehouse.A: Views encapsulate join logic, filters, and column selections into reusable queries, providing a consistent and reliable way to query data.

get-started-data-warehouse.Q: How do measures standardize business calculations in reports and dashboards?
get-started-data-warehouse.A: Measures define reusable DAX expressions for calculations, ensuring consistency and serving as a single source of truth for metrics.

get-started-data-warehouse.Q: What is the advantage of using Direct Lake mode for semantic models in Power BI?
get-started-data-warehouse.A: It reads data directly from OneLake Parquet files, reflecting the latest warehouse data without requiring scheduled refreshes and avoiding storage and processing overhead.

get-started-data-warehouse.Q: What is the first layer of access control in a Fabric data warehouse?
get-started-data-warehouse.A: Workspace roles.

get-started-data-warehouse.Q: What permission is required at a minimum for a user to connect using the SQL analytics endpoint?
get-started-data-warehouse.A: Read permission.

get-started-data-warehouse.Q: What does Row-Level Security (RLS) in a Fabric data warehouse do?
get-started-data-warehouse.A: It restricts which rows a user can see using WHERE clause predicates.

get-started-data-warehouse.Q: What is the purpose of Query Insights in a Fabric data warehouse?
get-started-data-warehouse.A: It provides a central location for historical query data and actionable performance information.

get-started-data-warehouse.Q: Which system view in Query Insights returns information about each completed SQL request?
get-started-data-warehouse.A: queryinsights.exec_requests_history.

get-started-data-warehouse.Q: What is the purpose of Dynamic Management Views (DMVs) in a Fabric data warehouse?
get-started-data-warehouse.A: To monitor active connections, sessions, and requests in real time.

get-started-kusto-fabric.Q: What type of data processing does Real-Time Intelligence in Microsoft Fabric enable?
get-started-kusto-fabric.A: It enables processing and analyzing data as events occur, rather than in batch mode.

get-started-kusto-fabric.Q: What is a key benefit of using Real-Time Intelligence for monitoring delivery performance?
get-started-kusto-fabric.A: It allows for immediate detection of delays and issues, enabling faster response and customer updates.

get-started-kusto-fabric.Q: What are some data sources that can be used with Real-Time Intelligence in a delivery company scenario?
get-started-kusto-fabric.A: GPS trackers, package scanning systems, and customer notification platforms.

get-started-kusto-fabric.Q: How does Real-Time Intelligence differ from traditional batch processing?
get-started-kusto-fabric.A: Real-Time Intelligence processes and analyzes data as it is generated, while batch processing analyzes data in historical snapshots.

get-started-kusto-fabric.Q: What is one use case for Real-Time Intelligence in delivery operations?
get-started-kusto-fabric.A: Spotting route delays quickly and estimating delivery windows based on current conditions.

get-started-kusto-fabric.Q: What is real-time analytics?
get-started-kusto-fabric.A: Real-time analytics is the practice of processing, analyzing, and acting on data as it's generated, typically within seconds to minutes of when events occur.

get-started-kusto-fabric.Q: What is an event in the context of real-time analytics?
get-started-kusto-fabric.A: An event is a record of something that happens in a system, such as a website click or a stock price change.

get-started-kusto-fabric.Q: What is a stream in real-time analytics?
get-started-kusto-fabric.A: A stream is a sequence of events, typically ordered by the time an event occurred, that flows continuously as events happen.

get-started-kusto-fabric.Q: What are the components of real-time analytics solutions?
get-started-kusto-fabric.A: The components include real-time data ingestion, stream processing, low-latency storage, interactive dashboards, and automated decision making.

get-started-kusto-fabric.Q: What is the purpose of stream processing in real-time analytics?
get-started-kusto-fabric.A: Stream processing transforms and analyzes data while it flows, including filtering, aggregating, and detecting patterns with minimal latency.

get-started-kusto-fabric.Q: What are the benefits of real-time analytics?
get-started-kusto-fabric.A: Benefits include responding immediately to opportunities or problems, optimizing operations, enhancing customer experiences, and preventing issues by detecting anomalies.

get-started-kusto-fabric.Q: What is Real-Time Intelligence in Microsoft Fabric?
get-started-kusto-fabric.A: Real-Time Intelligence in Microsoft Fabric is a platform that integrates components like Eventstreams, Eventhouses, Real-Time Dashboards, and Activator to enable real-time data monitoring, analysis, and action.

get-started-kusto-fabric.Q: What is the purpose of Real-Time Intelligence in Microsoft Fabric?
get-started-kusto-fabric.A: To process, analyze, and act on data in motion with minimal latency, enabling near real-time insights.

get-started-kusto-fabric.Q: What are Eventstreams used for in Real-Time Intelligence?
get-started-kusto-fabric.A: Eventstreams are used to capture streaming data from various sources and apply real-time transformations as data flows through the system.

get-started-kusto-fabric.Q: What type of database is used in Eventhouses for storing real-time data?
get-started-kusto-fabric.A: KQL (Kusto Query Language) databases are used in Eventhouses for storing real-time data.

get-started-kusto-fabric.Q: What is the function of the KQL Queryset in Real-Time Intelligence?
get-started-kusto-fabric.A: KQL Queryset provides a workspace for running and managing queries against KQL databases, supporting both KQL and T-SQL syntax.

get-started-kusto-fabric.Q: How do Real-Time Dashboards in Microsoft Fabric function?
get-started-kusto-fabric.A: Real-Time Dashboards connect directly to KQL databases, refresh automatically as new data arrives, and allow interactive exploration of data.

get-started-kusto-fabric.Q: What is the role of Activator in Real-Time Intelligence?
get-started-kusto-fabric.A: Activator monitors streaming data against user-defined rules and thresholds to trigger automated actions such as notifications or workflows.

get-started-kusto-fabric.Q: What is the Real-Time hub in Microsoft Fabric?
get-started-kusto-fabric.A: The Real-Time hub is a central location to discover and manage streaming data, connect to data sources, and subscribe to events for real-time analytics.

get-started-kusto-fabric.Q: What types of sources can be connected to the Real-Time hub?
get-started-kusto-fabric.A: Sources such as Azure IoT Hub, Azure Service Bus, Azure Data Explorer DB, database change data capture feeds, and external cloud providers can be connected.

get-started-kusto-fabric.Q: What are the two primary approaches for ingesting streaming data in Microsoft Fabric?
get-started-kusto-fabric.A: Using eventstreams or directly ingesting data into a KQL database in an Eventhouse.

get-started-kusto-fabric.Q: What are the three main components of an Eventstream in Microsoft Fabric?
get-started-kusto-fabric.A: Sources, transformations, and destinations.

get-started-kusto-fabric.Q: Name two Microsoft sources that can be connected as data sources for an Eventstream.
get-started-kusto-fabric.A: Azure Event Hubs and Azure IoT Hubs.

get-started-kusto-fabric.Q: What is the purpose of transformations in an Eventstream?
get-started-kusto-fabric.A: To filter, summarize, and reshape raw data into a useful and actionable format before storage.

get-started-kusto-fabric.Q: List two examples of transformations available in Eventstreams.
get-started-kusto-fabric.A: SQL code and aggregate.

get-started-kusto-fabric.Q: What are some possible destinations for data processed by an Eventstream?
get-started-kusto-fabric.A: A KQL database in an Eventhouse, Lakehouse, a derived stream, Fabric Activator, or a custom endpoint.

get-started-kusto-fabric.Q: What is the difference between transformations in Eventstreams and update policies in a KQL database?
get-started-kusto-fabric.A: Transformations in Eventstreams occur during stream processing, while update policies in a KQL database are triggered after data is written to a table.

get-started-kusto-fabric.Q: What is the role of update policies in a KQL database?
get-started-kusto-fabric.A: They are automation mechanisms that transform ingested data by running a query when new data is written to a table.

get-started-kusto-fabric.Q: What is the purpose of KQL databases in an Eventhouse?
get-started-kusto-fabric.A: KQL databases are used to store and query real-time data that flows from Eventstreams and other streaming sources.

get-started-kusto-fabric.Q: What language is used to query data in KQL databases?
get-started-kusto-fabric.A: Kusto Query Language (KQL) or a subset of Transact-SQL (T-SQL).

get-started-kusto-fabric.Q: What are KQL querysets?
get-started-kusto-fabric.A: KQL querysets are collections of KQL queries used to work with data in KQL database tables.

get-started-kusto-fabric.Q: What type of data is KQL optimized for?
get-started-kusto-fabric.A: KQL is optimized for analyzing large volumes of structured, semi-structured, and unstructured data, particularly time-series data.

get-started-kusto-fabric.Q: What is an example of a KQL query to retrieve 10 rows from a table named 'stock'?
get-started-kusto-fabric.A:
```kql
stock
| take 10
```

get-started-kusto-fabric.Q: What is a materialized view in the context of KQL databases?
get-started-kusto-fabric.A: A materialized view is a precalculated and stored summary result for faster queries.

get-started-kusto-fabric.Q: Can you use T-SQL to query KQL databases in Eventhouses?
get-started-kusto-fabric.A: Yes, KQL databases support a subset of common T-SQL expressions.

get-started-kusto-fabric.Q: What is the role of Copilot in Microsoft Fabric Eventhouses?
get-started-kusto-fabric.A: Copilot helps write queries to extract insights from Eventhouse data using AI.

get-started-kusto-fabric.Q: What is the purpose of a Real-Time Dashboard in Microsoft Fabric?
get-started-kusto-fabric.A: To pin data visualizations to a single visual interface, enabling real-time insights at a glance.

get-started-kusto-fabric.Q: What is a tile in the context of a Real-Time Dashboard?
get-started-kusto-fabric.A: A tile is a component of a dashboard that shows information based on a KQL query extracting real-time data from tables in an eventhouse.

get-started-kusto-fabric.Q: How can you create a Real-Time Dashboard in Microsoft Fabric?
get-started-kusto-fabric.A: You can create it in a workspace and configure its source, or directly from a KQL queryset in an eventhouse.

get-started-kusto-fabric.Q: What is the default visualization type for a tile in a Real-Time Dashboard?
get-started-kusto-fabric.A: The default visualization type is a table showing the results of the query.

get-started-kusto-fabric.Q: What interactive features do tiles in a Real-Time Dashboard offer?
get-started-kusto-fabric.A: Tiles allow data exploration through drilling into the data, filtering, aggregating, and changing the visualization type.

get-started-kusto-fabric.Q: Can you create Power BI reports from KQL database data in Microsoft Fabric?
get-started-kusto-fabric.A: Yes, you can create Power BI reports from KQL database data.

get-started-kusto-fabric.Q: What is the purpose of Microsoft Fabric's Activator?
get-started-kusto-fabric.A: Activator enables automated processing of events to trigger actions based on specific conditions.

get-started-kusto-fabric.Q: What are the four core concepts of Activator?
get-started-kusto-fabric.A: Events, Objects, Properties, and Rules.

get-started-kusto-fabric.Q: In Activator, what does an 'Event' represent?
get-started-kusto-fabric.A: An event represents a record in a stream of data that has occurred at a specific point in time.

get-started-kusto-fabric.Q: What is an 'Object' in the context of Activator?
get-started-kusto-fabric.A: An object is a representation of a business entity, such as a sales order or a sensor, based on the data in an event record.

get-started-kusto-fabric.Q: What are 'Properties' in Activator?
get-started-kusto-fabric.A: Properties are fields in the event data mapped to aspects of the state of a business object, such as a temperature or total amount.

get-started-kusto-fabric.Q: What is the role of 'Rules' in Activator?
get-started-kusto-fabric.A: Rules define conditions under which actions are triggered based on the property values of objects referenced in events.

get-started-kusto-fabric.Q: Provide an example of a use case for Activator.
get-started-kusto-fabric.A: Sending a notification when the temperature measured by a sensor exceeds a specific threshold.

get-started-kusto-fabric.Q: How can Activator be used in dynamic inventory management?
get-started-kusto-fabric.A: Activator can trigger actions such as initiating marketing campaigns when product sales drop or alerting managers about inventory shortages.

What makes an eventhouse suitable for real-time monitoring?

choose-data-store-fabric.Q: Which Fabric data store is recommended for machine learning workloads?
Why is a dedicated lakehouse recommended for machine learning workloads?

design-dimensional-models-fabric.Q: What is the primary purpose of dimensional modeling in analytical data stores?
design-dimensional-models-fabric.A: To structure data for efficient querying, filtering, and aggregation.

design-dimensional-models-fabric.Q: What are the two main types of schema used in dimensional modeling?
design-dimensional-models-fabric.A: Star schema and snowflake schema.

design-dimensional-models-fabric.Q: What is the role of fact tables in dimensional modeling?
design-dimensional-models-fabric.A: To capture business events and store quantitative data for analysis.

design-dimensional-models-fabric.Q: What is the role of dimension tables in dimensional modeling?
design-dimensional-models-fabric.A: To organize descriptive attributes that provide context to the data in fact tables.

design-dimensional-models-fabric.Q: What is a common challenge addressed by dimensional modeling regarding data changes over time?
design-dimensional-models-fabric.A: Managing slowly changing dimensions.

design-dimensional-models-fabric.Q: What is the primary purpose of dimensional modeling?
design-dimensional-models-fabric.A: To organize data for analytical workloads, prioritizing query performance and user comprehension.

design-dimensional-models-fabric.Q: What are the two types of tables in a dimensional model?
design-dimensional-models-fabric.A: Fact tables and dimension tables.

design-dimensional-models-fabric.Q: What do fact tables store in a dimensional model?
design-dimensional-models-fabric.A: Measurements associated with business events or observations, such as sales amounts or order quantities.

design-dimensional-models-fabric.Q: What do dimension tables represent in a dimensional model?
design-dimensional-models-fabric.A: Entities relevant to analytics requirements, such as products, customers, dates, or locations.

design-dimensional-models-fabric.Q: What is the main advantage of a star schema?
design-dimensional-models-fabric.A: It simplifies queries by reducing the number of joins, is intuitive for users, and supports semantic models in Power BI.

design-dimensional-models-fabric.Q: When should you consider using a snowflake schema?
design-dimensional-models-fabric.A: When dimensions are extremely large, require shared hierarchies, or need keys for different levels of granularity.

design-dimensional-models-fabric.Q: What is a tradeoff of using a snowflake schema?
design-dimensional-models-fabric.A: It requires more joins, which can reduce query performance and add complexity to queries.

design-dimensional-models-fabric.Q: Why is a star schema recommended for Power BI semantic models?
design-dimensional-models-fabric.A: Because it provides a clear structure that supports Copilot and AI scenarios, and aligns with how users think about data.

design-dimensional-models-fabric.Q: What are the three types of columns in a fact table?
design-dimensional-models-fabric.A: Dimension keys, measures, and attributes.

design-dimensional-models-fabric.Q: What does the grain of a fact table specify?
design-dimensional-models-fabric.A: The grain specifies what one row in the fact table represents.

design-dimensional-models-fabric.Q: What is a transaction fact table used for?
design-dimensional-models-fabric.A: A transaction fact table stores one row per business event, typically at the lowest possible granularity.

design-dimensional-models-fabric.Q: What is the purpose of a periodic snapshot fact table?
design-dimensional-models-fabric.A: To capture the state of something at regular intervals, useful for trend analysis.

design-dimensional-models-fabric.Q: What is an accumulating snapshot fact table?
design-dimensional-models-fabric.A: A fact table that tracks the progress of a process through milestones, updating rows as milestones are reached.

design-dimensional-models-fabric.Q: What are the three types of measure aggregation?
design-dimensional-models-fabric.A: Additive, semi-additive, and non-additive.

design-dimensional-models-fabric.Q: What is a factless fact table?
design-dimensional-models-fabric.A: A table that records events without numeric measures, useful for analyzing occurrences by counting rows.

design-dimensional-models-fabric.Q: What is an aggregate fact table?
design-dimensional-models-fabric.A: A table that stores precomputed summaries of a base fact table at a higher granularity or lower dimensionality to accelerate queries.

design-dimensional-models-fabric.Q: What is the purpose of a surrogate key in a dimension table?
design-dimensional-models-fabric.A: A surrogate key is a system-generated unique identifier that serves as the primary key, insulating the data warehouse from changes in source systems and enabling historical tracking.

design-dimensional-models-fabric.Q: Why is denormalization recommended for dimension tables?
design-dimensional-models-fabric.A: Denormalization improves performance by reducing the need for joins, enabling faster queries and simpler filtering and grouping in reports.

design-dimensional-models-fabric.Q: What is a conformed dimension?
design-dimensional-models-fabric.A: A conformed dimension is shared across multiple fact tables, ensuring consistency in analysis and comparison across different business processes.

design-dimensional-models-fabric.Q: What is a role-playing dimension?
design-dimensional-models-fabric.A: A role-playing dimension is a single dimension table referenced multiple times in a fact table, each reference representing a different context or role.

design-dimensional-models-fabric.Q: What is the purpose of a junk dimension?
design-dimensional-models-fabric.A: A junk dimension consolidates many small, independent dimensions with low cardinality into a single table, reducing the number of dimension tables and foreign keys in the fact table.

design-dimensional-models-fabric.Q: What is a balanced hierarchy?
design-dimensional-models-fabric.A: A balanced hierarchy has the same number of levels in every branch, such as a calendar hierarchy with year, quarter, month, and day.

design-dimensional-models-fabric.Q: What naming convention is typically used for dimension tables in a Fabric Warehouse?
design-dimensional-models-fabric.A: Dimension table names are typically prefixed with 'd_' or 'Dim_', such as 'd_Product' or 'Dim_Customer'.

design-dimensional-models-fabric.Q: What is the difference between a surrogate key and a natural key in a dimension table?
design-dimensional-models-fabric.A: A surrogate key is a system-generated unique identifier used as the primary key, while a natural key is the identifier from the source system used to link the dimension back to its source data.

design-dimensional-models-fabric.Q: What is the purpose of Slowly Changing Dimension (SCD) patterns in a data warehouse?
design-dimensional-models-fabric.A: SCD patterns define how a dimensional model responds to changes in source data to accurately describe the past.

design-dimensional-models-fabric.Q: What is the characteristic of a Type 0 SCD?
design-dimensional-models-fabric.A: Type 0 retains the original value and does not allow changes, suitable for fixed reference data.

design-dimensional-models-fabric.Q: When is a Type 1 SCD appropriate?
design-dimensional-models-fabric.A: Type 1 is used when the change is a correction to an error or historical accuracy for the changed attribute is not important.

design-dimensional-models-fabric.Q: How does a Type 2 SCD handle changes?
design-dimensional-models-fabric.A: Type 2 inserts a new row for each change, maintaining full history with additional columns like start date, end date, and current flag.

design-dimensional-models-fabric.Q: What is the difference between Type 2 and Type 3 SCDs?
design-dimensional-models-fabric.A: Type 2 maintains full history by adding rows, while Type 3 tracks limited history by adding columns for current and previous values.

design-dimensional-models-fabric.Q: What does a Type 6 SCD combine?
design-dimensional-models-fabric.A: Type 6 combines Type 1, Type 2, and Type 3 to maintain full history, current value, and previous value on every row.

design-dimensional-models-fabric.Q: What SCD type is recommended for fixed reference data that never changes?
design-dimensional-models-fabric.A: Type 0.

design-dimensional-models-fabric.Q: What are the tradeoffs of using Type 2 SCDs?
design-dimensional-models-fabric.A: Type 2 increases storage requirements, adds query complexity, and requires sophisticated ETL logic.

design-dimensional-models-fabric.Q: What is the purpose of a star schema dimensional model in a Fabric Warehouse?
design-dimensional-models-fabric.A: To analyze sales performance across dimensions such as stores, products, customers, and time periods.

design-dimensional-models-fabric.Q: What types of tables are created in a star schema dimensional model?
design-dimensional-models-fabric.A: Fact tables and dimension tables.

design-dimensional-models-fabric.Q: What is a Slowly Changing Dimension (SCD) pattern used for in a star schema?
design-dimensional-models-fabric.A: To manage changes in dimension data over time while preserving historical accuracy.

fabric-transform-data-dataflows.Q: What is the purpose of data transformation in analytics?

fabric-transform-data-dataflows.Q: What are the benefits of using Dataflows Gen2 for data preparation?

fabric-transform-data-dataflows.Q: What types of destinations can Dataflows Gen2 load transformed data into?
fabric-transform-data-dataflows.A: Dataflows Gen2 can load transformed data into lakehouses, warehouses, and other Fabric destinations.

fabric-transform-data-dataflows.Q: How can Dataflows Gen2 benefit a team with members experienced in Power Query?
fabric-transform-data-dataflows.A: Team members can leverage their Power Query skills to create reusable transformation logic for data preparation.

fabric-transform-data-dataflows.Q: What is the primary purpose of Dataflows Gen2 in Microsoft Fabric?
fabric-transform-data-dataflows.A: Dataflows Gen2 are cloud-based ETL tools that use Power Query to connect to data sources, apply transformations, and load results to a destination.

fabric-transform-data-dataflows.Q: Which interface do Dataflows Gen2 use for building transformation logic?
fabric-transform-data-dataflows.A: Dataflows Gen2 use the Power Query Online interface for building transformation logic.

fabric-transform-data-dataflows.Q: What are the three update methods available when configuring a destination for a Dataflow Gen2?
fabric-transform-data-dataflows.A: The three update methods are Replace, Append, and Incremental refresh.

fabric-transform-data-dataflows.Q: What are some key destinations supported by Dataflows Gen2?
fabric-transform-data-dataflows.A: Key destinations include Fabric Lakehouse, Fabric Warehouse, Azure SQL Database, Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2, and Snowflake.

fabric-transform-data-dataflows.Q: When should you consider using Dataflows Gen2 over other tools?
fabric-transform-data-dataflows.A: You should use Dataflows Gen2 when you prefer low-code solutions, need reusable transformation logic, or require loading transformed data to multiple destinations.

fabric-transform-data-dataflows.Q: What is the difference between Replace and Append update methods in Dataflows Gen2?
fabric-transform-data-dataflows.A: Replace drops and recreates the destination with every refresh, while Append adds new rows to the existing destination without removing previous data.

fabric-transform-data-dataflows.Q: What is the advantage of using Incremental refresh in Dataflows Gen2?
fabric-transform-data-dataflows.A: Incremental refresh refreshes only new or changed data, significantly reducing refresh time and resource consumption for large datasets.

fabric-transform-data-dataflows.Q: What is a scenario where Dataflows Gen2 might not be the best choice?
fabric-transform-data-dataflows.A: Dataflows Gen2 might not be the best choice for complex transformations requiring code, large-scale data processing, or when full T-SQL is needed.

fabric-transform-data-dataflows.Q: What is the primary tool used to transform data in Power Query Online?

fabric-transform-data-dataflows.Q: How do you create a new dataflow in a Fabric workspace?

fabric-transform-data-dataflows.Q: What are the five main areas of the Power Query Online editor?

fabric-transform-data-dataflows.Q: What is the purpose of the 'Applied Steps' section in the Query settings pane?

fabric-transform-data-dataflows.Q: What transformation would you use in Power Query to combine values from multiple columns?

fabric-transform-data-dataflows.Q: What is the M language used for in Power Query?

fabric-transform-data-dataflows.Q: What feature in Power Query allows you to use natural language prompts to generate transformation logic?

fabric-transform-data-dataflows.Q: What is the Modern Query Evaluator in Dataflow Gen2?
fabric-transform-data-dataflows.A: The Modern Query Evaluator is a feature in Dataflow Gen2 that improves performance and reliability for Power Query transformations by optimizing common shaping patterns.

fabric-transform-data-dataflows.Q: What is query folding in Power Query?
fabric-transform-data-dataflows.A: Query folding is the process of pushing transformation logic from Power Query to the data source for execution, allowing the data source to perform the transformations.

fabric-transform-data-dataflows.Q: What are the three possible outcomes of query folding evaluation?
fabric-transform-data-dataflows.A: The three outcomes are full folding, partial folding, and no folding.

fabric-transform-data-dataflows.Q: Which transformations typically support query folding?
fabric-transform-data-dataflows.A: Transformations such as filtering rows, selecting/removing columns, sorting rows, grouping and aggregating, merging queries from the same source, changing data types, and renaming columns typically support query folding.

fabric-transform-data-dataflows.Q: How can you check if a step in Power Query folds?
fabric-transform-data-dataflows.A: Right-click the step in the Applied Steps pane and look for the 'View Native Query' option. If it is available, the step folds; if it is grayed out, it does not fold.

fabric-transform-data-dataflows.Q: What are preview-only steps in Power Query?
fabric-transform-data-dataflows.A: Preview-only steps are transformations that run during data preview and authoring validation but are excluded from final execution during refresh.

fabric-transform-data-dataflows.Q: What is the benefit of using staging dataflows?
fabric-transform-data-dataflows.A: Staging dataflows separate extraction from transformation, allowing for independent refresh schedules, reuse of staged data, and availability of raw data for reprocessing.

fabric-transform-data-dataflows.Q: What are the two approaches for parameterization in Dataflow Gen2?

fabric-transform-data-dataflows.Q: What tool is used to apply transformations in a Dataflow Gen2?

fabric-transform-data-notebooks.Q: What is the primary purpose of notebooks in Microsoft Fabric?
fabric-transform-data-notebooks.A: To provide an interactive, code-based environment powered by Apache Spark for data transformation.

fabric-transform-data-notebooks.Q: Which two programming languages can be used in Fabric notebooks for data transformation?

fabric-transform-data-notebooks.Q: What are some common tasks you can perform with Fabric notebooks?

fabric-transform-data-notebooks.Q: What is the underlying engine that powers Fabric notebooks?
fabric-transform-data-notebooks.A: Apache Spark.

fabric-transform-data-notebooks.Q: What type of tables do you write transformed results to in Fabric notebooks?

fabric-transform-data-notebooks.Q: What is the advantage of using Spark SQL in Fabric notebooks?

fabric-transform-data-notebooks.Q: What is PySpark's DataFrame API used for in Fabric notebooks?

fabric-transform-data-notebooks.Q: What is the primary computing engine that Fabric notebooks run on?

fabric-transform-data-notebooks.Q: What are the two types of cells in a Fabric notebook?
fabric-transform-data-notebooks.A: Code cells and markdown cells.

fabric-transform-data-notebooks.Q: What is the purpose of pinning a default lakehouse in a Fabric notebook?

fabric-transform-data-notebooks.Q: What command allows switching languages within a Fabric notebook?
fabric-transform-data-notebooks.A: Magic commands, such as `%%sql` for Spark SQL.

fabric-transform-data-notebooks.Q: When should you prefer using notebooks over Dataflows Gen2?
